lines: \paragraph{CV as pruning tolerance predictor.}

CV measures the dispersion of token importance under the L2-norm proxy. High CV indicates that some tokens carry substantially larger norms than others; these high-norm tokens can be identified and retained while low-norm tokens are removed with limited information loss. Low CV indicates near-uniform norms: no token subset is dispensable because all tokens contribute comparably. Pruning a low-CV model is equivalent to downsampling a uniform signal, where the spatial pattern of removal matters more than which specific tokens are selected by importance.

-CV also predicts the \emph{optimal pruning strategy}, not only the tolerance ceiling. When CV is low ($< 0.15$), L2-norm ranking captures spatial artifacts rather than genuine importance differences, and random selection outperforms L2 by preserving spatial coverage. When CV is high ($> 0.20$), L2-norm ranking exploits real importance differentiation and outperforms random. lines: Attention-based scoring functions estimate token importance from the LLM's internal attention weights. Three principal variants exist: (i)~\emph{column-sum scoring} sums each vision token's received attention weight in the last transformer layer, capturing direct query-key dependencies at the final processing stage; (ii)~\emph{cross-layer mean scoring} averages column-sum scores across all layers, aggregating importance signals over the full transformer stack; (iii)~\emph{attention rollout} multiplies attention matrices layer by layer (adding identity matrices for residual connections) to approximate cumulative information flow from input tokens to the output. Their primary limitation is computational: they require a full LLM forward pass and are backbone-specific. -Hard pruning fails for token-entangling connectors because removing any token destroys spatially distributed information. +Hard pruning fails for token-entangling connectors because removing any token destroys spatially distributed information. VTR addresses this through learned re-encoding rather than deletion.
+\paragraph{Architecture.}

+VTR inserts a 2-layer cross-attention module between the vision connector output and the LLM backbone input. Each layer uses 12 attention heads with dropout 0.1. A set of $M$ learned query vectors attends over all $N$ source tokens via standard multi-head cross-attention, producing $M$ compressed tokens as input to the LLM. The compression ratio is controlled by $M \in \{16, 32, 64, 96, 128\}$; $M{=}N$ serves as a passthrough control.

+The module adds ${\sim}$22M trainable parameters ($<$5\% of SmolVLA, the smallest VLA tested) and is trained end-to-end: compressor and action head parameters are jointly optimized. Architecture and training hyperparameters are detailed in Appendix~\ref{app:vtr_architecture}.
